Add TaskMaster with bounded storage and list support, then route list and

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: Use enums for date and month names
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace parallel weekday and month name lists with domain-specific enums.

- Keep accepted full names and abbreviations with their parsed values
- Simplify stream-based weekday and month lookups
- Preserve existing date parsing behavior

Rename vague variables and accessors across the parser, task, storage,
CLI, GUI, and test code.

Update related Javadocs and test call sites while preserving existing
application behavior.

The date parser handled relative dates, weekday prefixes, and

multiple absolute date formats in one long method, making the

happy path difficult to follow and increasing maintenance risk.

Extract relative-date resolution, weekday-prefix removal, and

absolute-expression parsing into focused helpers. Keep the

public parsing behavior unchanged while making each method easier

to understand and test.

The firstValidDay helper used nested conditionals to search the

current month and the following two months. Although correct, the

deeply nested branches obscure the normal successful path and make

the three-month search harder to verify.

Replace the nested branches with a bounded loop that checks each

candidate month in order and returns immediately when the requested

day exists. Preserve the existing invalid-date behavior when no

candidate month is suitable while making the control flow easier to

read and maintain.

The main date-time parsing method handled year-only, time-only,

date-and-time, and date-only inputs in one procedure. Mixing these

cases made the method longer than necessary and required readers to

track several parsing paths at once.

Extract each input shape into a focused helper while keeping the

top-level method as a high-level sequence of parsing stages. Preserve

the existing precedence rules, default times, and relative-date

behavior so this readability refactoring does not alter the parser's

accepted inputs or results.

The markTaskDone and unmarkTaskUndone operations duplicated the

same persistence and rollback sequence. Keeping those sequences in

parallel made future changes more likely to update one path but not

the other.

Extract the shared status transition, save, and rollback behavior

into updateTaskStatus while keeping the public methods as clear

named operations. Preserve task-number validation, storage failure

recovery, idempotent status changes, and existing user-facing results.

The command parser combined input validation, tokenisation, command

lookup, and command construction in one method. That mixed several

levels of abstraction and made the command-building path harder to

scan as more commands were added.

Extract input preparation, command-name resolution, and command

construction into focused helpers. Keep the explicit switch as the

single command-dispatch point, preserving all existing validation

messages, command arguments, and parsed command behavior.

CsvSaver.load combined file access, CSV parsing, header validation,

task reconstruction, and storage-error translation in one method.

This made the loading workflow harder to read and coupled file I/O

details to domain-object creation.

Keep load focused on locating the file and translating I/O failures.

Move record reading into readCsvRecords and task reconstruction into

createTasks. Preserve missing-file handling, header validation, task

validation, and all existing storage exceptions while using the

requested createTasks name for the conversion stage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge: Clean up code after three merges
commitResults.messageBody:
The recent branch merges left the stream-based CSV loader alongside obsolete loading helpers, causing the codebase to reference ArrayList without importing it. Remove the unreachable helpers so CsvSaver has one clear loading path and compiles cleanly.

Add a dedicated SE-EDU code-quality skill, require Checkstyle in the Java coding-standard workflow, and update AGENTS.md so future code changes are reviewed consistently for style, documentation, maintainability, and test coverage.

Implement B-Snooze support for postponing and rescheduling timed tasks.

- Add snooze and resched command parsing and execution.

- Support duration-based and explicit datetime updates.

- Reject ToDos and invalid or inconsistent time inputs.

- Preserve task status and roll back changes when saving fails.

- Update JUnit tests, CLI UI tests, and user documentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add decimal and combined snooze durations
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend snooze duration parsing beyond single integer units so users can combine calendar and clock components in canonical order.

- Support decimal minutes, hours, and days.
- Represent calendar and clock amounts with DurationPeriod.
- Reject unsupported, duplicate, negative, and non-canonical inputs.
- Preserve deadline/event validation and rollback behavior.
- Update unit tests, CLI UI scenarios, and user documentation.

Allow users to specify snooze durations with compact unit forms such as 1h, 1hr, 1min, 1mo, and 1yr.

- Centralize duration aliases in DurationPeriodUnit.
- Support optional whitespace and case-insensitive unit forms.
- Reject ambiguous, repeated, non-canonical, and adjacent components.
- Give decimal month and year values a dedicated user-facing error.
- Update duration tests, CLI UI scenarios, and documentation.

Support common natural-language expressions for snooze durations while

retaining the existing numeric and abbreviated forms.

- Add week units and canonical week ordering.

- Parse number words, optional "more" filler, and half-unit phrases.

- Preserve existing validation and dedicated calendar-decimal errors.

- Include invalid duration inputs in quoted error messages.

- Update duration tests, CLI UI scenarios, and user documentation.

Improve code organization by separating parsing responsibilities and

centralizing user-facing message templates.

- Extract duration input preparation, component parsing, validation, and

  accumulation into focused helpers.

- Reuse DurationPeriodUnit for natural-language duration aliases.

- Store invalid-duration message formatting with other UI messages.

- Rename date/time parser helpers to distinguish parsing, resolution,

  alternative handling, lookup, and formatter application.

- Align DateTimeParser Javadocs with the parser abstraction hierarchy.

- Rename firstValidDay to findValidDay for clearer intent.

- Update JUnit tests, CLI UI scenarios, documentation, and Javadocs.

- Preserve existing duration formats, validation rules, and output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add partial and flexible event rescheduling
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend event rescheduling to support updating either the start time or the end time independently, while preserving the omitted time.

- Accept event rescheduling with only /from or /to.
- Allow /from and /to markers in either order.
- Resolve time-only end values against the effective event start.
- Validate the final event time range before applying changes.
- Reject duplicate, unknown, and additional slash markers.
- Preserve task-type-specific validation and user-facing messages.
- Update parser tests, CLI UI scenarios, and documentation.

Strengthen persistence coverage for snoozing and rescheduling operations by verifying the exact CSV records written to storage.

- Test deadline and event snoozing by duration.
- Test explicit deadline and event snooze targets.
- Test full and partial event rescheduling.
- Verify standard CSV time-column ordering.
- Confirm event start times and task completion status are preserved.
- Reload saved tasks to verify storage round trips where practical.
- Keep the tests isolated with temporary CSV files.

Reject slashes at argument boundaries when they are followed by ASCII letters, while preserving ordinary slashes in descriptions and date formats.

- Centralize the ToDo invalid-format template.

- Validate marker boundaries using Java whitespace rules.

- Add parser and UI coverage for valid and invalid slash usage.

- Update the user guide with concise slash examples.

The root README does not describe the recently added timed-task commands or marker validation, leaving the user guide incomplete.

- Document snooze duration and explicit end-time forms.

- Document partial and reversed-order event rescheduling.

- Explain slash validation with valid and invalid examples.

- Reflect automatic persistence after snoozing and rescheduling.
Branch Snooze: Add Snooze and Rescheduling Support

Use boolean names that describe the conditions they represent.

- Rename the loading-state field to hasLoadError.

- Rename the constructor flag to hasLoadFailure.

- Use the public predicate during startup failure handling.

- Preserve existing loading behavior and accessor compatibility.

TaskMaster currently manages task storage, indexing, and CSV
projection alongside task operations, which mixes collection and
orchestration responsibilities.

- Make TaskList the owner of canonical indexed task storage.
- Move task numbering, views, mutations, and CSV projection into TaskList.
- Let TaskMaster delegate collection operations and retain orchestration,
  validation, persistence, and rollback.
- Update CsvSaver and tests for the new TaskList persistence boundary.

TaskMasterTest has grown into a large mixed-responsibility suite, while TaskList new ownership behavior needs direct coverage.

- Split TaskMaster tests into listing, mutation, scheduling, and
  persistence suites.
- Preserve existing TaskMaster behavior and rollback assertions.
- Retain TaskList coverage for validation, replacement, and views.
- Keep test names and Javadocs aligned with project conventions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task: Centralize timing validation and matching
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace task-type-specific scheduling paths with a shared immutable
timing value object and polymorphic task operations.

- Add TaskTimes factories for ToDo, deadline, and event schedules.
- Centralize timing-shape validation and date matching in TaskTimes.
- Store deadline and event timing through TaskTimes.
- Replace rescheduleDeadline and rescheduleEvent with rescheduleTask.
- Reuse TaskTimes snapshots for snooze and rescheduling rollback.
- Simplify LuckyNoReschedCommand and CSV task reconstruction.
- Extend task, scheduling, persistence, and timing tests.
- Preserve existing commands, messages, validation, and storage behavior.

The CLI behavior is currently covered mainly by documented manual test cases, which makes regressions harder to detect consistently.

Add Java-backed fixtures that execute all documented CLI scenarios in isolated working directories with deterministic time settings. Integrate the suite as the clitest Gradle task and make check depend on it.

Update the UI test plan and add a checklist for tracking future testing improvements.

Replace Arial with bundled Patrick Hand across the JavaFX interface and use bundled Roboto Mono for task display lines. Render task lines in dark code-style blocks, add regression coverage, and update the GUI test plan.

Track the completed typography work and remaining personality improvements in the project checklist.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Refine conversation and add checklist
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI needs to present real LuckyNoSlacky responses in the approved conversational layout while keeping warnings visually distinct and avatars reusable.

Refine the JavaFX dialogue rows, response severity handling, responsive styling, tests, and platform configuration, then record completed and remaining work in the improvements checklist.

Snooze durations can exceed LocalDateTime's supported range, which previously produced a generic format response for deadlines and could escape validation for events.\n\nValidate the computed end time for every timed task and return the dedicated overflow message. Cover both task types and document the CLI behavior.

Wrap filesystem security failures in storage exceptions so callers receive controlled errors instead of uncaught runtime failures.\n\nReport temporary-file cleanup failures, preserve primary save failures, and add deterministic coverage for filesystem access boundaries.

commitResults.messageBody:
Add accessible labels and help text for the conversation history, command field, and warning responses.

Apply the Pineapple Pop, clover-green, light-blue user, and dark-blue Send palette while keeping semantic response tones and supplied avatars consistent.\n\nRender each multiline reply as one bubble and group task lines into a dark Roboto Mono panel. commitResults.messageTitle: Test: Expand task model edge-case coverage
commitResults.messageBody: Expand tests for timing invariants, status transitions, task-list indexing, capacity limits, whitespace handling, and exact validation messages.\n\nAdd small-capacity overflow tests and update the testing-improvement checklist to record the completed coverage.

The window opens directly into the conversation without a clear brand identity.\n\nAdd a fixed yellow header with the supplied chatbot avatar, title, tagline, and green clover accent. Add GUI regression coverage and update the related test plan and improvement checklist.

Continue in degraded mode when task storage cannot be loaded.\n\nShow the existing warning while retaining an empty in-memory task list so the CLI and GUI remain usable. Allow subsequent task mutations to save normally, and add deterministic CLI and GUI coverage for the recovery path.

Expand rollback, reload, malformed CSV, capacity, and physical-size coverage for task persistence.\n\nVerify persisted records semantically and assert exact storage error messages. Update the testing-improvement checklist accordingly.

Reject task additions when the task list reaches its maximum capacity.\n\nShow a friendly centralized message while keeping the CLI and GUI usable. Preserve the existing task list, avoid unnecessary saves, and add coverage for all task-creation commands and interface recovery.

Separate chatbot speaker roles from response tones so command results can use distinct visual treatments without changing message text or CLI output.

Classify command responses as neutral, success, info, warning, or system error; add clover, warning, and system-error markers; and update GUI tests, plans, and documentation.

The conversation area needs a subtle lucky visual identity without changing the approved header, message colours, task rendering, or controls.\n\nAdd a bundled transparent clover tile over a pale-green conversation viewport, with GUI/resource regression coverage and updated documentation.

Report malformed `luckynoslacky.fixedNow` values without exposing an uncaught exception or non-zero exit.

Show the friendly configuration message, pause briefly for readability, and add coverage for valid, blank, and invalid clock configuration.

Expand tests for fixed-clock configuration, startup load failures, CLI termination, and GUI parse and save error responses.

Use isolated subprocess probes for filesystem-dependent scenarios, add EOF coverage to the UI plan, and update the testing-improvement checklist.
